\MakeContractTitle{Scientific Rationale}{%
  A rigorous astronomer-facing derivation of the v0.1 detector-sample
  transformation, its atmosphere and response conditions, its uncertainty
  meaning, and the claims that available authority does and does not support.}

\DraftNotice

\begin{abstract}
SCI-CAL v0.1 calibrates an admitted ordinary \code{xs} detector sample to a
top-of-atmosphere point-source-peak \(\mjybeam\) convention. The absolute
factor is the selected immutable measured APT row's \code{flxscale}, applied
once. Any TolProj pointing-derived correction is either already embodied in
that selected factor or unresolved; it is never blindly multiplied again.
The target-observation atmosphere correction is a distinct positive factor at
the full eligible-sample airmass and top-of-atmosphere pivot. Conditional
measurement covariance transforms with the same realized operator, while
calibration, atmosphere, and response systematics remain separate correlated
nuisance terms. The point-source-peak label remains conditional on the
originating Beammap response and separately realized downstream response.

The retained atmosphere operator is structurally adopted, but the authorized
packet does not supply its content-bound numeric nodes, ordinate orientation,
or numeric support. This document therefore fixes the structural mathematics
and truthful no-output behavior while withholding numeric atmosphere and
calibrated numeric output authorization until one precise owner decision is
resolved. Even after that decision, a structural pass is only
\code{science-qualification-eligible}; any achieved
\code{science-qualified} or \code{calibrated-science} claim remains subject to
the separate evidence threshold in this authority.
\end{abstract}

\section{Scientific purpose and authority boundary}
\label{sec:sci-purpose}

The scientific problem is not merely to multiply a timestream by a number. It
is to state which detector occurrence the number belongs to, what physical
role it has, where its calibration reference plane lies, which atmosphere
state applies at the target sample, what response gives meaning to
\(\mjybeam\), which uncertainty is transformed, and which claims remain
unsupported.

The admitted author packet consists only of the approved SCI-CAL v0.1 Scope
Brief; its approved independent-core supersession cover together with the
frozen independent mathematical core at exact Git blob
\code{27b0916e725696597c3ba84fb6a82bf6cf0ea356}; the exact TolTECA v1 passband
authority manifest at Git blob
\code{8c581bfb26f01b187f4f1e0565f4457bcc25f099}; and the approved sanitized
conventions and ownership extract. No implementation, executable contract,
audit finding, repair, test, numerical execution, validation, Unity material,
or active ALIGN material informs this draft.

Later scope and cover decisions supersede the frozen core where they differ.
In particular, v0.1 is \code{xs}-only and \(\mjybeam\)-only; measured and
design identity are layered; a proven row relation is admissible; the retained
atmosphere result is structural rather than an empirical guarantee; and the
engineering-opacity class does not produce calibrated output.

\section{Boundary of the estimator}
\label{sec:sci-boundary}

Upstream authorities provide the admitted signal and sample eligibility,
target acquisition identity, exact selected measured APT and association,
calibration quantities and lineage, opacity and airmass inputs, requested mode,
conditional measurement uncertainty when available, and response identities.
SCI-CAL does not select an APT, perform matching, infer a beam, estimate
pointing, choose an atmosphere estimator, make a map, design a filter, or
validate empirical response.

The endpoint is a calibrated detector sample on valid support, transformed
conditional variance/weight or covariance where one exists, a coherent
validity/quality state, a nuisance-completeness ledger, and resolvable canonical
lineage. Maps and fitted source products are downstream consumers.

The central causal distinction is:
\begin{equation*}
 \underbrace{\text{source Beammap evidence}\longrightarrow
 F^{\rm sel}}_{\text{selected immutable APT ancestry}}
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 \underbrace{(\tau_{225},X,\mathcal O_a)\longrightarrow C_a}_{
 \text{target-observation atmosphere}}
 \qquad\longrightarrow\qquad y.
\end{equation*}
The first branch establishes the detector's selected absolute scale. The
second corrects the current target sample to the same top-of-atmosphere plane.
Their provenance and uncertainty remain distinct even though their scalar
values multiply.

\section{Scientific interpretation of the factor algebra}
\label{sec:sci-factor-interpretation}

Equation~\eqref{eq:signal} is affine only because the upstream baseline state
is explicit. After conditioning on that state and the calibration state, the
operator is diagonal in sample and detector occurrence. It creates no time
convolution, spatial remapping, or additive sky signal. A time-dependent
atmosphere factor is amplitude modulation; it is not a stationary transfer
function.

The selected APT row is deliberately the absolute-factor boundary. If a
pointing-derived correction produced a child artifact, the value in that
child is the value used by SCI-CAL. Equation~\eqref{eq:embodied-pointing}
explains its ancestry, while Equation~\eqref{eq:once-only} prevents both using
the parent without the correction and multiplying the correction twice.
Relative \code{responsivity} and Beammap \code{sens} remain scientifically
useful quantities, but their names do not make them additional absolute flux
factors.

The multiplication is order independent only after factor roles have been
resolved. A list of anonymous scalars is not an equivalent representation:
two equal values can have different recipients, reference planes, correlation
scopes, and ancestry. Reconstructibility therefore depends on factor-instance
identity and causal lineage, not just the product \(M_j\).

\section{Atmosphere meaning and the limit of present authority}
\label{sec:sci-atmosphere}

The atmosphere portion uses zenith \(\tau_{225}\) and full sample airmass to
form the line-of-sight coordinate in Equation~\eqref{eq:los-coordinate}. The
retained operator, rather than an assumed generic exponential, supplies a
band-dependent transmission or correction. The node orientation matters:
linear interpolation of transmission followed by inversion is not generally
equal to linear interpolation of correction. That is why
Equation~\eqref{eq:operator-orientation} makes the missing orientation an
authority field rather than a software choice.

The structural adoption is strong: zero opacity is exactly unity, positive
opacity has no unity plateau, direction is monotonic, node values are exact,
and seams are continuous. It is also deliberately bounded. A sample must lie
in the intersection of opacity policy, upstream airmass validity, operator
node support, and opacity time support. Bracketing permits only a named source-
authorized interpolation; it never licenses endpoint extrapolation.

No calibrated numeric output or numeric
\code{science-qualification-eligible} disposition can presently be derived
from this packet because the actual node record, its orientation, and its
numeric support are absent. Supplying those facts would enable structural
evaluation only. Unless the owner later defines a different explicit
threshold, an achieved \code{science-qualified} or
\code{calibrated-science} claim additionally requires separately accepted
atmosphere-representation-fidelity and observational-performance evidence over
the same declared identity and support. The passband record is a content-bound
modeled array reference, not a measured telescope response, and has no
supplied uncertainty or settled photon-versus-energy semantics. Those
limitations condition any future representation study and keep associated
nuisance uncertainty unavailable.

The segment opacity classes are policy states, not model claims. A fully
admitted segment within \(0\leq\tau_{225}\leq0.15\) may attain only the
structural state \code{science-qualification-eligible}. It does not thereby
attain science qualification. A segment entering
\(0.15<\tau_{225}\leq0.25\) has an engineering-availability label but no v0.1
calibrated output because no continuous engineering operator is adopted.
Larger, missing, malformed, or out-of-support inputs are outside calibrated
scope.

\section{Uncertainty interpretation}
\label{sec:sci-uncertainty}

Equations~\eqref{eq:conditional-covariance} and
\eqref{eq:variance-weight} are exact conditional transformations. They answer
the question: if calibration, atmosphere, response, selection, and identity
state were fixed, how would measurement noise transform? They do not answer
how uncertain that state is.

The nuisance model answers the second question. Detector \code{flxscale}, a
common calibrator scale, any embodied pointing-derived correction, atmosphere
and WVR modeling, approximate \code{sens}-based weights, passband limitations,
and beam/template response have different recipients and correlation scopes.
Equation~\eqref{eq:nuisance-covariance} preserves those scopes. In particular,
Equation~\eqref{eq:common-rank-one} shows why a common systematic does not
average down with the number of samples. A conditional inverse-variance weight
therefore cannot be called total calibrated uncertainty or statistical
significance while required nuisance terms are unavailable.

First-order propagation is useful only locally. The atmosphere interpolant is
continuous but may not be differentiable at its seams; large, asymmetric, or
seam-spanning uncertainty cannot be summarized by one local derivative.
Association and support are discrete. Fitted calibration state can share data
with the signal. These cases require posterior samples, nonlinear propagation,
or an explicit bounded sensitivity study rather than silent zero cross terms.

\section{Response interpretation}
\label{sec:sci-response}

The calibrated detector sample carries the originating Beammap beam/template
identity so that a downstream consumer knows the response basis of its
point-source-peak convention. It does not claim that a particular mapmaker,
kernel, or filter realizes that basis. Equation~\eqref{eq:peak-response}
exposes the conditional statement: the ideal peak is the source flux only
when the downstream response has unit peak for the declared template.

A response-changing kernel can be entirely valid engineering while changing
the scientific meaning of the peak. The remedy is to measure or calculate its
response under the owning downstream contract, propagate an explicit
renormalization if appropriate, and update provenance. It is not to preserve
the old label by assumption. Similarly, retaining elliptical parameters does
not authorize surface-brightness or integrated-flux conversion; those are
future contracts.

\section{Validity and honest scientific claims}
\label{sec:sci-validity}

The tuple in Equation~\eqref{eq:validity-tuple} prevents one failure mode from
being hidden inside another. Intentional disablement is not invalid input.
Valid signal with missing nuisance uncertainty is not zero uncertainty.
Engineering-only opacity is not science-qualification-eligible. Eligibility
itself is not achieved science qualification. Structurally correct calibration
is not proof of atmosphere truth or telescope performance. A machine-readable
reason must make each distinction visible to downstream scientists.

The canonical lineage record makes these claims reproducible. It identifies
the raw observation, selected APT bytes and semantics, occurrence association,
factor ancestry, atmosphere/passband/operator, reference plane, units,
uncertainty states, and response basis. Compact products can point to that
record, but the linkage must resolve all inputs needed to reconstruct
Equation~\eqref{eq:reconstruction}.

\section{Scientific conclusion}
\label{sec:sci-conclusion}

The v0.1 scientific operation is the once-only transformation in
Equations~\eqref{eq:multiplier} and \eqref{eq:signal}, conditioned on the
layered identity, support, and response definitions above. It preserves a
sharp separation between conditional measurement noise and correlated
calibration/response systematics, and between structural correctness,
atmosphere representation fidelity, and observational performance.

The strongest defensible draft stops short of numeric atmosphere
authorization. One content-bound operator decision is required before a
calibrated numeric sample or numeric \Term{science-qualification-eligible}
disposition can be produced. Even after that decision, actual
\code{science-qualified} or \code{calibrated-science} status requires the
separately accepted representation-fidelity and observational-performance
evidence stated in \Req{049}, unless the owner later defines a different
explicit threshold. The present limitation is a scientific result of the
information boundary, not an invitation to select a legacy fallback or infer
missing nodes.
